AI is changing how we work, create, research, and grow businesses.

You no longer need dozens of hours or complicated software to complete everyday tasks. The right AI tools can help you work smarter, save time, and improve productivity.

Here are 8 categories of AI tools that can make your workflow more efficient.

1. AI Tools for Creating — Turn Ideas Into Content

Create stunning visuals, images, and creative assets with AI.

Useful tools:

- Midjourney — AI image generation.
- DALL·E — Create images from text prompts.
- Runway — AI-powered creative generation.

Best for designers, creators, and marketers.

2. AI Tools for Writing — Create Better Content

Generate ideas, write articles, improve grammar, and create professional content.

Useful tools:

- ChatGPT — Writing and brainstorming.
- Jasper — AI marketing content.
- Grammarly — Writing and editing assistance.

Best for bloggers, professionals, and content creators.

3. AI Tools for Design — Create Professional Visuals

Design presentations, graphics, and marketing materials without starting from scratch.

Useful tools:

- Canva — Graphic design and presentations.
- Adobe Firefly — AI-powered creative design.
- Figma AI — Design and interface workflows.

Best for designers, startups, and businesses.

4. AI Tools for Editing — Transform Your Media

Make video and audio editing faster with AI-powered features.

Useful tools:

- Descript — Audio and video editing.
- Pictory — Convert content into videos.
- CapCut — AI-powered video editing.

Best for YouTubers, video editors, and social media creators.

5. AI Tools for Research — Find Information Faster

Research complex topics, discover insights, and explore reliable information.

Useful tools:

- Perplexity — AI-powered research.
- Elicit — Research paper discovery and analysis.
- Consensus — Research-backed answers.

Best for students, researchers, and professionals.

6. AI Tools for Marketing — Grow Your Brand

Plan campaigns, create marketing content, and improve your online presence.

Useful tools:

- https://t.co/cJrTD6yk0y — Marketing copy generation.
- https://t.co/7nlQqjjdtO — Social media content creation.
- Surfer SEO — SEO content optimization.

Best for marketers, agencies, and business owners.

7. AI Tools for Automation — Eliminate Repetitive Work

Connect different applications and automate everyday workflows.

Useful tools:

- Zapier — Connect apps and automate tasks.
- Make — Build visual automation workflows.
- n8n — Create advanced automated workflows.

Best for businesses, freelancers, and productivity-focused teams.

8. AI Tools for Analysis — Turn Data Into Insights

Understand complex information, analyze datasets, and make better decisions.

Useful tools:

- ChatGPT — Data analysis.
- Julius AI — Analyze data using natural language.
- Tableau — Data visualization and business intelligence.

Best for analysts, business owners, and data professionals.

You don't need to master every AI tool. Start with the ones that solve your biggest problems.

3 very interesting papers i read on rl for robotics, each one builds on top of the other

1. omnireset by @patrickhyin
instead of starting every episode from the beginning, start from all over the task: reaching, holding the part, part half inserted. on a real robot, zero shot from cameras, it got 85% on peg insertion. diffusion policy with 100 real demos got ~2%

2. sgs (success guided sampling) by @octi_zhang 
omnireset picks those starting points at random. but a lot of them are either too easy (robot always succeeds) or too hard (always fails), and the robot learns nothing from either. sgs tracks how often the robot succeeds from each starting point and practices mostly on the ones it gets right about half the time. on screwing a nut onto a bolt in sim, success went from 6% to 70%

3. alphanist by @octi_zhang 
uses both, but the only reward is 1 when the part is fully assembled. one policy learns all 20 tasks on the nist assembly board at 98% in sim. 20 separate policies got 81% with 39x the compute, and adding the usual shaped reward dropped it to 18%

none of this needed human demos or reward tuning, just better choices about where training starts. feels like rl for manipulation is way more underrated than people think right now
